coverage: SQLite and native pg_dump/pg_restore to brand-new roots apply actual account/child deletion receipts before the restore guard becomes ready. Private originals, page/checkpoint directories, source-bound working JSON and ended/revoked upload chunks are removed.

Shared-family source SHA, shared child material, a frozen PDF with no mutable material record, valid pending upload and a legitimate queued PDF job remain usable. Fresh login, real upload completion and actual three-page processing succeed after restore.
Every asset generation advances, former deleting ownership is cleared and stale source/collection tasks are fenced. Old login tokens fail; rebuilt permanent revocations reject late writes.
Old lease/purge/staging metadata is omitted from the new root. A current active upload conflicting with an old permanent revocation fails closed rather than restoring write permission.
Complete current reference and file inventories are checked before unlink. Every source deletion is checked against the verified manifest and file identity; unrelated administrator bytes survive.

Unknown verified-backup files remain, an injected directory junction during copying is not chmodded or deleted through, and an interrupted cleanup after one unlink leaves both restore guards pending. Existing target overwrite is refused; the same original backup/ledger can restore into a different empty root.

Frozen PDF originals are included in both backup formats even when only course snapshots retain the SHA. Actual bytes are hashed before their size is recorded. Explicit material sizes remain authoritative; frozen text of unspecified historical format is not guessed to require a TXT file.
